title: A generically fibre-trivial line on a smooth integral-fibre family comes from the base
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field] and let $S$ and $Y$ be regular integral separated schemes of finite type over $k$ [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-regular-scheme, def-pc-integral-scheme, def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Separated means that the diagonal is a closed immersion. Let $f:Y\to S$ be a smooth surjective morphism [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms] with nonempty geometrically integral fibres, meaning that $Y\times_S\operatorname{Spec}L$ is integral for every point $s\in S$ and every field extension $L/\kappa(s)$. Write $\eta=\operatorname{Spec}k(S)$ for the generic point of $S$, where $k(S)$ is the fraction field of any nonempty affine coordinate ring, and put $Y_\eta=Y\times_S\eta$ [def-pc-fibre-product]. Let $M$ be an invertible $\mathcal O_Y$-module [def-sc-invertible-module]. If $M|_{Y_\eta}\simeq\mathcal O_{Y_\eta}$, there exist an invertible $\mathcal O_S$-module $N$ and an isomorphism $f^*N\simeq M$. The pullback is ordinary tensor pullback of sheaves of modules [def-pc-module-pullback].

source.place: Tag 00ON (lemma-dimension-base-fibre-equals-total), applied to a vertical prime divisor of a smooth morphism; divisors.tex Tag 0AGA (lemma-weil-divisor-is-cartier-UFD) and more-algebra.tex Tag 0AG0 (lemma-regular-local-UFD). proof.text: By the definition of regular scheme [def-weil-regular-scheme], both $S$ and $Y$ are locally Noetherian. Apply clause (1) of [rem-pc-regular-normal] to the regular scheme $S$: every local ring of $S$ is an integrally closed domain. Thus $S$ is normal, and it is integral by hypothesis. These are hypotheses (1) and (2) of Stacks Tag 0BD7.

source.place: Tag 0BD7, lemma-in-image-pullback, hypotheses (1)--(2); properties.tex Tag 0569, lemma-regular-normal

proof.text: By [lem-pc-smooth-flat], $f$ is flat and locally of finite presentation. In the affine presentation of [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation], each point $y\in Y$ has affine opens $U=\operatorname{Spec}A\ni y$ and $V=\operatorname{Spec}R\supseteq f(U)$ with $A\cong R[x_1,\ldots,x_n]/(g_1,\ldots,g_m)$, so $A$ is generated over $R$ by the images of the $x_i$ and $R\to A$ is of finite type. This is the pointwise condition of [lem-weil-pbc-lft-pointwise-criterion], which therefore shows that $f$ is locally of finite type in the sense of [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. For each $s\in S$, use the given geometric-integrality condition with the identity extension $L=\kappa(s)$: the residue-field fibre $Y_s$ is integral and nonempty. This verifies hypotheses (3) and the locally-of-finite-type alternative in (4) of Tag 0BD7.

source.place: Tag 0BD7, lemma-in-image-pullback, hypotheses (3)--(4); morphisms.tex Tags 01VE and 01VF, lemma-smooth-locally-finite-presentation and lemma-smooth-flat; morphisms.tex Tag 01T2, lemma-locally-finite-type-characterize

proof.text: By [lem-sc-integral-function-field-affine-fraction], the generic stalk $\mathcal O_{S,\eta}$ is the fraction field of the coordinate ring of every nonempty affine open of $S$. Thus the generic fibre in [lem-sfb-normal-noetherian-generic-line-pullback] is the $Y_\eta$ in the statement. Its required tensor-pullback triviality is exactly the assumed $M|_{Y_\eta}\simeq\mathcal O_{Y_\eta}$. Apply that lemma with $T=S$, $Y=Y$, $f=f$, and $M=M$, using the hypotheses verified in steps 1--2. It gives an invertible $\mathcal O_S$-module $N$ and $f^*N\cong M$, with ordinary tensor pullback, as required.
